scope: source review, AST comparison and bounded temporary-root tests; no owner root, model, science workload or production adoption

independent_test.scope: real small Python children and temporary execution roots only

independent_ast_result.method: AST dump comparison of top-level functions in new execution.py against pinned queue-v3 execution.py
independent_ast_result.launch_and_reservation_note: launch, lock, inspect, supervise, child_main, terminal validation, recover, stop and collection function ASTs are unchanged; their calls now pass through source-bound load/registered checks. Runtime fixtures cover success, nonzero exit, retry, live worker, unknown recovery and stop cleanup.

verified_contract: Preparation calls across different cycle/job keys serialize through one ownership.lock. Under that lock, immutable-by-convention output and attempt/job claims are scanned before new claims; output path equality or component containment in either direction rejects, while lexical siblings remain available.

The intent is atomically published/fsynced before attempt/scaffold files. Intent records the exact spec, store binding and job-lock identity. Crashes after intent and at five scaffold stages retain the output/job claim and exact replay repairs only matching content without launch; changed specifications and nested contenders fail.

Concurrent tests cover both conflict orientations, exact collision, identical exact replay and nonoverlapping siblings. For same conflicting claims only one process succeeds; identical replay returns the same prepared receipt with one intent.

Store identity binds absolute root and exact execution/ledger/receipt source pins; old/unadopted roots, mixed imports, alternate module paths and source drift fail closed in tests. Existing queue finite-run V1/V2 stores are separate and unchanged.

explicit_negative_boundary.reproduction: test_external_deletion_of_sole_intent_is_documented_limit: child exits immediately after publishing the only durable intent and before attempt/output/job claims; external deletion of that intent allows a nested output claim to be prepared.
explicit_negative_boundary.interpretation: A cooperating process crash alone leaves the fsynced intent for repair. Deleting it is an external filesystem mutation; this exact negative case means the registry is not self-healing or independently witnessed if a sole pre-scaffold intent is lost. It is acknowledged, not a passing security property.
explicit_negative_boundary.mitigation_needed_if_in_scope: Use a second independent durable witness or store-level append-only/integrity mechanism; same mutable root and same owner cannot protect against coherent removal/rollback.

limits: The global lock coordinates only successor clients for one execution root. Legacy/original managers, other roots and noncooperating writers can bypass it. No migration/adoption of existing execution roots occurs.

Output directory containment is an ownership namespace check; it does not sandbox child code that writes outside its declared root. Symlink/namespace mutation after canonical validation and hostile same-user changes are not prevented.

The registry is owner-writable JSON; no external append-only witness, hostile-owner security, power-loss/fsync ambiguity proof, disk-full/NFS behavior, exhaustive schedule, full original regression suite or scale benchmark is supplied. Pairwise scans are quadratic in retained intents.
Tests are small fixtures, not production work. No scientific qualification or thousands-cycle capability follows.
